historical_record.description: The Art Commission approved the final drawings for the Laurel Hill Playground, Collins Street and Euclid Avenue, designed by Ryan and Lee, Architects.

Under the 1947 recreation bond program the Recreation and Park Commission engaged Paul A. Ryan and John Michael Lee, architects, to design the playground ($100,000) and field house ($30,000) on the Laurel Hill Playground site at Collins Street and Euclid Avenue.

The Recreation and Park Commission awarded the contract to build Laurel Hill Playground and its field house to S & Q Construction Co. at $165,327, subject to funds, and asked for a further $22,997 from the 1947 recreation bond fund to cover it.

The Recreation and Park Commission approved Open Space plans to rehabilitate Laurel Hill Playground on Euclid near the Laurel Heights Shopping Center, with wooden climbing structures, drainage repairs, security lighting so the clubhouse could be used at night, and seating in the plaza between the clubhouse and play area.
The Recreation and Park Commission awarded J.M. Construction a $94,843 contract to rehabilitate Laurel Hill Playground.
